C1.rule: Mechanical, one owned file, fully specified, no design choice

C2.rule: Bounded implementation or tests, clear spec, one or two owned files and their tests

C3.rule: Cross-module design; changes a gate or the ledger contract; wrong means every project inherits it

C4.rule: Planning, merging, reconciling, anything in a project's real data, a sponsor decision

items.title: Must-read under 3,000 words: card replaces raw ledger, OPERATING-RULES folds into HANDOFF, checkpoint stays
items.what: Lead's decision on the two open questions from the 15 Sep rules review (A-18, A-19), made because the sponsor asked for a recommendation rather than a number: target 3,000 words, not the reviewer's 2,500. Reasoning: the checkpoint is the one file that says what is actually in flight right now, which is exactly what a resumed or reheated lead must not miss -- dropping it from the mandatory read to save ~860 words risks the silent-gap failure the checkpoint exists to prevent, so it stays mandatory. The cheaper cut with no information loss is merging docs/OPERATING-RULES.md into HANDOFF.md as one file: M-09 already dedupes the rules the two files repeat, so folding what is left costs nothing and removes a whole file from the read order. Card-only ledger reading (A-19) is adopted outright: bin/warmup's card is generated from the ledger and already the compressed form (~1,061 words against ~37,672 for the raw JSON across 11 proposals); every read-order line that says 'read the ledger(s)' means the card, with the full ledger JSON opened only for the item currently being worked. Structure: CLAUDE.md, HANDOFF.md (absorbing OPERATING-RULES), the warmup card, the latest checkpoint, CLAUDE-workflow.md cut to one line per rule (M-10). M-09 and M-10 do the trimming; this item sets the target and the structure they trim to. Priority order, the sponsor's own ruling: nothing important is dropped to hit the word count -- 3,000 is the target, not a ceiling that outranks completeness. Cutting duplication, dead rationale and raw-ledger-in-favour-of-the-card loses no information, so it is done regardless. If what is left after that still carries something a lead needs and is still over 3,000, it stays and the count is reported as what it is, not trimmed further to hit the number.
items.done: A fresh lead's mandatory read -- CLAUDE.md + HANDOFF.md (merged) + the warmup card + the latest checkpoint + CLAUDE-workflow.md -- is 3,000 words or fewer, measured by the same word count the review used; every read-order line across docs/OPERATING-RULES.md (folded in), templates/lead-prompt.md and skills/warmup says 'the warmup card' where it used to say 'the ledger(s)'; docs/OPERATING-RULES.md no longer exists as a separate file, or is a pointer to HANDOFF.md if removing it outright breaks too much; if 3,000 cannot be reached without cutting the checkpoint, a prohibition, or anything else a lead needs to not miss something important, the item is not blocked over it -- it is closed with the real word count and a one-line note of what stayed and why, because completeness outranks the number.

log.evidence: Card replaces raw ledger in read order; OPERATING-RULES.md folded into HANDOFF.md; checkpoint stays mandatory. Real word count reported honestly (over 3,000; completeness prioritized per sponsor ruling). Commit 1144fe9.
